author: Shazmeen Navrange
title: Massive Netflix Talent Leaving After 7 Years - NewsBreak
text:
By Shazmeen Navrange ,
38 minutes ago Photo Credit: Netflix A Netflix talent, who served as the VP and Head of Live Experiences, is stepping down from his position. He has served the streaming giant since July 2019.
Greg Lombardo is leaving as Netflix VP of Global Experiences Greg Lombardo, after serving for 7 years as VP and Head of Live Experiences, is now leaving the streaming service. The reason behind his departure and who will be replacing him currently remain publicly undisclosed. Since joining Netflix, he has been involved in many major initiatives, including key projects like creating Netflix Houses, brick-and-mortar venues in Philadelphia and Dallas.
These venues have offered fans live entertainment and dining experiences inspired by beloved Netflix movies and shows. This includes experiences from renowned projects like Stranger Things, Wednesday, Squid Game, Bridgerton, and K-Pop Demon Hunters, among many others.
In addition, Lombardo was also involved in the creation of Queen’s Ball: A Bridgerton Experience and the upcoming K-Pop Demon Hunters world tour. In his recent role, he used to report to the VP and GM of Global Experiences, Mitzi Reaugh. Before joining Netflix, he was a CEO at Offshore Surf and Senior Vice President at Fox Filmed Entertainment, per his LinkedIn . In a conversation with Blooloop , he also appreciated his time as a Creative Director at BRC Imagination Arts, calling it a significant one for his field knowledge.
“My location-based experience started with BRC Imagination Arts, a commercial production house in Burbank. I ran the brand group for them. This was a terrific learning experience, working on great branded entertainment projects,” he elaborated. His latest departure from the streaming giant follows that of Pam Levine, who served as VP of Marketing and Publicity for the U.S. and Canada. She had been a part of the streaming giant since last year. It remains unclear what Lombardo’s next career move will be following his exit.
